statusDetail: Coverage-complete audit of six representative paths; account-only post-login, payment completion, authenticated bookmarking, and real network-offline mutation were not covered because they require credentials/payment or destructive external conditions.

page.notes: SSR content/catalog site with interactive React/Astro islands, installable manifest, public chapter reader, and account/subscription surfaces.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Light/dark captures are visually equivalent and computed color-scheme is normal.
Ten animations remain running under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.
No contrast-preference rule was found and Lighthouse confirms low-contrast text/control tokens.
No View Transition CSS or startViewTransition use was found in DOM/CSS or 42 bundles.
No parallax, scrollytelling, or scroll-linked reveal interaction was present on the representative paths.
checkOutcomes.reason: The site has scrolling but no scroll-linked animation use case to implement.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Homepage carousels use CSS scroll-snap/overscroll behavior, preserving native scrolling mechanics.
Very long homepage/reader surfaces have no scroll-state signal or progress affordance.
Menus exist, but no CSS anchor positioning signal is shipped.
Clear cards, section headings, chapter links, and visible 404 recovery actions preserve navigation context.
The mobile subscription promotion consumes most of the initial viewport before core content.
Detail disclosure uses custom buttons; no details/dialog primitives are present.
Content cards dominate the desktop layout and the chapter reader removes global chrome to prioritize the comic.
All five mobile archetypes report 360px content/viewport widths and zero horizontal overflow; viewport scaling remains enabled.
Reusable content components adapt globally, but no @container/container-type implementation is present.
Focused login input has no visible focus style, and reader controls are as small as 24x24/28.7x16.
Homepage H1 states the reading offer; comic cards and detail “First Chapter” action expose the next step.
A user can navigate from home to detail to a full current chapter without authentication; the audited chapter rendered all 30 comic images.
Invalid URLs produce a purposeful 404 with Return Home and Browse Comics; empty login submission gets native required-field recovery.
Lighthouse LCP is 14.2–15.8s on content paths and CLS is 0.498–1.666.
Homepage and reader shifts exceed good CLS limits; unsized images are named as culprits.
Trace reports no long tasks and 0ms TBT on home; Lighthouse TBT is 0ms home/detail and 12ms chapter.
Home transfers 4.36MB, includes a 2.21MB hero image, weak CDN caching, and pervasive missing dimensions/srcset.
Lighthouse identifies about 24KiB unused client JS and home requests 42 scripts.
Lighthouse finds accessible-name mismatches and prohibited ARIA on a roleless detail div.
Lighthouse finds contrast ratios from 2.13:1 to 4.05:1 on detail, reader, and login.
Homepage heading order skips levels and keyboard-focused login input has no visible outline/shadow.
Screenshots show readable line lengths and unclipped body text across desktop and mobile content templates.
Viewport permits scaling and layouts reflow, but several reader controls are materially below comfortable target size.
Lighthouse best-practices scores 1.0 on all four audited templates and reports no console-error audit failure.
Doctype/charset are valid, but 79/80 homepage images and all sampled chapter panels omit explicit dimensions.
Lighthouse best-practices is 1.0 on home, detail, chapter, and login; no prompt-on-load or deprecated-platform failure appeared.
Public home/detail/chapter pages have descriptive titles and descriptions; login is intentionally private/noindex.
Links use real hrefs, viewport meta allows scaling, robots allows public routes, and Lighthouse SEO is 1.0 on public samples.
Public pages return successfully with canonicals; robots references a valid sitemap index and only private areas are disallowed.
Home exposes Organization/WebSite JSON-LD and detail exposes Breadcrumb, Article, ComicSeries, Open Graph, and image metadata.
HTTPS/HSTS/nosniff pass, but CSP and other key policies are missing.
No known trackers, third-party cookies, or exposed secrets were found; cross-origin hosts are owned CDN/API surfaces.
No on-load permission prompt was observed, but an applicable authentication flow has no passkey/WebAuthn implementation signal.
HSTS/nosniff are present, but clickjacking, CSP, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy defenses are absent.
Raw HTML contains 93% of rendered content words with title, H1, and description intact; it is not a JS shell.
Representative menus/cards remain within responsive layouts, disclosure toggling completes repeatedly, and no runtime error failure appeared.
The site declares a standalone installable manifest but registers no service worker or offline fallback.
A deliberately invalid URL returns a useful branded recovery state with two clear routes back to content.
html lang=en is present and CSS inspection finds extensive inline logical properties rather than only left/right layout.
Relative date strings are rendered, but no Intl.RelativeTimeFormat/DateTimeFormat signal exists in 42 loaded bundles.
The audited public reading, catalog, and login flows do not schedule events or ask users to enter/coordinate wall-clock times.
checkOutcomes.reason: No time-zone-sensitive event or scheduling use case exists on the representative paths.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Subscription pricing and monthly commitment are stated plainly; promotion is dismissible and public reading does not require subscription.
Required inputs validate after attempted submission with native, field-specific “Please fill in this field” recovery.
Email/password/sign-up inputs omit autocomplete tokens.
Audited surfaces show explicit $2.99/month pricing, no yearly commitment, a forgot-password route, and separate sign-up/log-in choices.
47 homepage images are oversized, 62 lack responsive sources, and Lighthouse estimates multi-megabyte image savings.
Home requests 42 scripts and ships avoidable unused client code even though main-thread blocking remains low.
A single chapter load reaches 27.4MB and eagerly loads all 30 chapter panels plus comment/profile media.
No declared agent-facing intent or transactional agent capability was found; public content remains machine-readable via SSR and metadata.
checkOutcomes.reason: Agent capabilities are emerging/contextual and this public reader does not signal an agent-tool surface.

checkOutcomes.evidence: No summarisation, generation, or other inference feature exists in the representative user journeys.
checkOutcomes.reason: There is no inference use case for which on-device AI could be evaluated.

checkOutcomes.evidence: After 20 description toggles, heap self size fell from 10,271,788 to 10,032,105 bytes; node count rose only 1.8%, without a Detached constructor signal.
Detail heap is about 10.3MB self size and 152k nodes, proportionate to a media-rich hydrated detail page.
Baseline/post summaries contain no Detached constructor among retained populations and total heap does not grow after repeated disclosure.

paths.description: Homepage and discovery surface: navigation, subscription banner, hero carousel, trending and latest content.
Browse/listing archetype representing catalog filtering and repeated comic cards.
Comic detail archetype representing description disclosure, bookmarking, chapter discovery, and offline-download entry.
Primary reading journey: a current chapter with long-form image content, navigation, reactions, and comments.
Authentication form archetype: labels, validation, focus, autofill, recovery, and modern-auth support.
Recovery path for an invalid URL, representing intentional HTTP error handling.

findings.summary: The fixed dark palette does not respond to the user’s color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: Light and dark emulation produce the same dark surface, while the platform probe reports computed color-scheme: normal.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light/dark tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Animations continue when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, getAnimations() still reports ten running animations, including repeated 2-second effects and an 8-second effect; no reduced-motion rule was found.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce override that removes non-essential animation and stops auto-advance.

findings.summary: Route and state changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The CSS/DOM and 42 loaded script bundles contain no view-transition signal or startViewTransition call.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document and cross-document View Transitions for route changes and substantial state swaps, with reduced-motion fallbacks.

findings.summary: Long listing and reader surfaces provide no scroll-state-aware navigation chrome.
findings.evidence: The homepage is 6,419px tall on mobile and the reader is 130,011px, but CSS inspection found no scroll-state query, progress indicator, or scroll-position signal.
findings.suggestedFix: Add lightweight scroll progress or scroll-state-aware controls to preserve orientation on long surfaces.

findings.summary: Menus and transient UI are not anchored with modern positioning primitives.
findings.evidence: The Resources/menu surface is present, but CSS and loaded bundles contain no anchor-name or position-anchor signal.
findings.suggestedFix: Use CSS anchor positioning and position-try fallbacks for menus/tooltips near viewport edges.

findings.summary: The subscription promotion dominates the first mobile viewport.
findings.evidence: At 360x800, the on-load Asura+ panel occupies roughly 440px before the primary comic content begins, despite being dismissible.
findings.suggestedFix: Collapse the promotion to a compact, persistent but non-blocking banner on mobile and remember dismissal.

findings.summary: Disclosure and overlay interactions use custom controls rather than semantic primitives.
findings.evidence: The detail page has two custom “Show more” buttons but zero details and zero dialog elements; no popover/dialog was found.
findings.suggestedFix: Use details/summary for description disclosure and popover/dialog for transient or modal UI with declarative dismissal.

findings.summary: Responsive components rely on viewport rules rather than container-level adaptation.
findings.evidence: The site reflows without horizontal overflow, but CSS and loaded bundles contain no @container/container-type signal across reusable card/list components.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container queries for reused cards, ranking panels, and detail controls while retaining a media-query fallback where needed.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly styled and several reader controls are undersized.
findings.evidence: Focusing the login email field reports outline-style none and no box shadow. Reader controls include 24x24 and 28.7x16 buttons, below comfortable touch-target sizing.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a strong :focus-visible ring and increase compact reader/comment controls to at least 44 CSS px or equivalent spacing.

findings.summary: Primary content pages have severe LCP and CLS failures.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured homepage LCP 15.85s/CLS 0.498, detail LCP 14.23s/CLS 0.505, and chapter LCP 15.81s/CLS 1.666. The mobile layout observer independently measured homepage CLS 0.5115.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve image geometry, remove the oversized hero dependency, prioritize only the true LCP image, and lazy-load below-fold reader/media assets.

findings.summary: Text and controls fail WCAG contrast on detail, reader, and login paths.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports ratios as low as 2.13:1 for reader Next, 3.3:1 for purple text, and 2.27:1 for the login OR separator against dark surfaces.
findings.suggestedFix: Raise muted and purple token contrast to at least 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for essential large/UI graphics; verify all states.

findings.summary: Image delivery is oversized, unsized, and poorly cached.
findings.evidence: HAR totals 4.36MB on home, including a 2.21MB hero cover. The image audit finds 79/80 images without dimensions, 47 oversized, and 62 without srcset; Lighthouse estimates 3.8MB savings and HAR finds many CDN images without useful cache headers.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve responsive srcset/sizes variants, use the 400px cover instead of the full source for blurred/thumbnail uses, add width/height or aspect-ratio, and set immutable caching on versioned CDN assets.

findings.summary: The page hydrates code that is not needed for first use.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates about 24KiB unused in client.D_Es0amM.js; the homepage requests 42 scripts even though trace TBT is currently 0ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Delay optional islands and load account, modal, comment, and download code only when the associated interaction is requested.

findings.summary: Accessible names, roles, and heading order are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse flags footer links whose visible labels do not match accessible names, an aria-label prohibited on a roleless div on detail, and a homepage heading-order skip.
findings.suggestedFix: Align accessible names with visible labels, replace the roleless labelled div with a semantic control, and make heading levels sequential.

findings.summary: Key browser-enforced security policies are missing.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive confirms HTTPS, HSTS, and nosniff, but finds no Content-Security-Policy, frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP with frame-ancestors, plus explicit Referrer-Policy and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Authentication has no passkey/WebAuthn path.
findings.evidence: The login flow offers password and Google sign-in, while both the page and all 42 loaded bundles contain no PublicKeyCredential or navigator.credentials signal.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey registration and authentication as a phishing-resistant option while retaining an account-recovery path.

findings.summary: The installable manifest has no service worker or offline fallback.
findings.evidence: manifest.json declares standalone display and app icons, but navigator.serviceWorker.getRegistrations() returns an empty list.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a service worker with a small app-shell/error fallback and deliberate caching for bookmarked/downloaded chapters.

findings.summary: Relative dates appear fixed to English with no locale-formatting implementation signal.
findings.evidence: The UI renders strings such as “1 day ago” and “last week”; inspection of all 42 loaded bundles finds no Intl.RelativeTimeFormat or Intl.DateTimeFormat.
findings.suggestedFix: Format dates with Intl.RelativeTimeFormat/DateTimeFormat using the active locale and expose absolute timestamps in semantic time elements.

findings.summary: Sign-in and sign-up fields omit autocomplete tokens.
findings.evidence: Both login and registration forms return empty autocomplete values for email, password, and confirm-password fields.
findings.suggestedFix: Use email, current-password, new-password, and username tokens as appropriate; keep labels and native input types.

findings.summary: The chapter reader eagerly transfers a disproportionate media payload.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports a 27,423KiB chapter load, including many 900x16,000 images and large profile/comment media; all 30 chapter images report loading=auto.
findings.suggestedFix: Virtualize or lazy-load chapter panels and comments near the viewport, generate display-sized variants, and defer avatars/GIF media until comments approach view.

taskList.title: Fix image sizing, responsive delivery, lazy loading, and cache policy
Restore visible keyboard focus and adequate target sizes
Deploy CSP and defensive response policies
Correct contrast and semantic accessibility defects
Reduce and conditionally load client JavaScript
Make the installable experience resilient offline
Add sign-in autofill and passkey support
Reduce mobile promotion dominance and use semantic disclosure
